title: How Can Noise Cancel Noise? #headphones #physics
description:
Noise-cancelling headphones don't block the noise: they add an upside-down copy of it, and the two add up to almost nothing at your ear. Half a cycle late, and the copy would double the noise instead.

Full episode: How do headphones cancel noise with more noise? https://youtu.be/rOxQ3PFvewk

Sources
- Elliott (2001), Signal Processing for Active Control, Academic Press
- Leventhall, A history of active noise control, Institute of Acoustics
- Cui, Behar, Kunov & Wong (2002), Canadian Acoustics 30(3)

subtitles: How can headphones make silence by adding sound?
The electronics don't block the noise.
Sound is a wave of squeezed and stretched air.
A tiny microphone listens to the noise.
The headphones play a copy, flipped upside down.
Where the noise squeezes the air, the copy stretches it.
Together they add up to almost nothing.
Half a cycle late, and the copy doubles the noise instead.
A low hum's cycle lasts just a few milliseconds.
Higher sounds are faster, so the timing gets harder.
That's why it works best on steady, low hums, like an engine, and less on voices.
